samples.question: The picture shows a white rectangular plate ruled into square rooms by thick black walls. Wherever a wall between two neighbouring rooms is missing, those two rooms are already joined and you can walk straight from one into the other; where a wall is drawn, you cannot. Walking from room to room through the missing walls, in as many steps as you like, joins the rooms into larger apartments, and the outer rim of the plate is walled all the way round. Three of the drawn walls each carry one shut door, painted as a short coloured bar across the wall - one orange, one purple and one teal. A shut door blocks the way just like the rest of the wall. Opening one door would cut a doorway through that one piece of wall only, joining whatever is on its two sides. One green dot and one red dot are painted flat on the floor, and they are not in the same apartment. Exactly one of the three doors, if it were opened, would make it possible to walk from the green dot to the red dot. Which door is it - orange, purple or teal?
